title: Hallway
textLines: You swallow hard, trying not to stare, trying not to think.
You don't know what this means — just that you have to keep moving.
Engineering might still hold answers.
You push yourself to your feet—
"Hey!"
The shout cracks through the silence behind you.
You spin around.
At the far end of the corridor, a figure steps out from the shadows — clothes scorched, face pale, eyes wide.
He's holding a wrench like a weapon, his stance defensive and disbelieving.
It's you.
"What did you do?" he barks, voice shaking. "What did you do to him?"
You glance down at the body, then back at him. "I—I didn't. I didn't mean to"
"That's a lie!" He takes a step closer, knuckles white around the wrench.
"There's a body on the floor and burn marks all over the wall.
You expect me to believe you just found him like that?"
"The gun was on stun!" you shout back. "It shouldn't have—"
He doesn't let you finish.
He lunges.
You stumble backward as the wrench swings past your face, clanging off the bulkhead.
The impact showers sparks into the air. You grab his arm, twist—he shoves you hard, both of you slamming into the wall.
The deck shudders beneath your boots, the sound of straining metal echoing through the hull.
"Stop!" you shout, grappling with him. "I'm you!"
For a heartbeat, he freezes—eyes locked with yours, breathing ragged.
He looks past you, at the corpse, at the burned features that could belong to either of you.
Then, slowly, his grip loosens. The wrench clatters to the floor.
The two of you stand there, panting, the hum of the ship filling the silence between heartbeats.
Finally, he speaks—voice rough, the fury drained into disbelief.
"I was in the cargo bay when the surge hit," he says. "Almost tore the hull apart.
I barely made it out before I had to eject the whole section."
He swallows, eyes flicking to the corpse. "I traced the power spike here… and then I found this."
You nod, still catching your breath. "I don't understand it either.
But if you were working on power, maybe we can finish what you started."
He hesitates, looking at you for a long, unreadable moment—like he's trying to decide if you're real.
Then he nods once.
"Fine. But stay where I can see you."
Together, you move down the corridor, leaving the corpse behind.
The ship groans around you — long, drawn-out, as if the hull itself is straining to hold.
The lights dim, then flare again, bathing everything in a sickly red glow.
For the first time, you both speak at the same time.
"This ship is dying."
Neither of you jumps. Neither of you disagrees.
You keep walking — side by side, two versions of the same person — toward Engineering.
— End of Part 1 —
